title: Modeling retinitis pigmentosa through patient-derived retinal organoids
protocol: Collect mid-stream urine samples from volunteers.
Transfer collected urine into 50-mL tubes using a 25-mL pipette.
Centrifuge the samples at 400 × g for 10 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Discard the supernatant carefully until 1 mL or less of liquid is left in the tube.
Resuspend and collect the liquid from one sample into a 50-mL tube.
Add 10 ml of washing buffer to dilute the samples.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 10 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Aspirate gelatin solution from cell culture plates and wash twice with washing buffer.
Add 1 mL of primary medium into each gelatin-coated well.
Resuspend the sediment in 1 mL of primary medium.
Transfer the cells onto gelatin-coated 6-well plates.
Incubate the plates.
Add 1 mL of the primary medium to the wells to maintain antibiotic and nutrition concentration.
Aspirate the culture medium until 1 mL is left in the wells.
Add 1 mL of proliferation medium.
Change half of the proliferation medium daily.
Aspirate 1 mL of the medium in the wells.
Add 1 mL of the proliferation medium.
Wash the cells twice using 1 mL of DPBS each time.
Dissociate the cells by adding 0.5 mL of TrypLE Select to each well.
Incubate the plates for 5 min at 37°C.
Add the medium containing 10% FBS to stop the reaction.
Centrifuge cells at 200 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend cells using the proliferation medium after removing the supernatant completely.
Seed the urinary cells in new gelatin-coated plates at a 1:4 split ratio for further expansion.
Add reprogramming plasmids (2 μg) encoding Oct4, Sox2, Lin28, Klf4, L-myc, p53shRNA, and the miR-302/367 cluster to the nucleofection solution.
Wash the urinary cells twice with DPBS.
Dissociate the cells to single cells using 0.5 mL of TrypLE Select.
Count the cells using a counting chamber.
Aspirate 105–106 cells for nucleofection.
Centrifuge cells at 200 × g for 3.5 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Aspirate the supernatant as much as possible by using pipette tips.
Resuspend cells in 100 μL of nucleofection solution.
Gently transfer the sample to Nucleocuvette vessels and tap the vessels to make sure the sample is at the bottom of the vessels.
Transfer the vessels to the retainer and electroporate them using the 4D-nucleofector system by using the T-020 program.
After the electroporation procedure, gently transfer the urinary cells into Matrigel-coated plates containing TeSR-E8 medium.
Change the medium after 24 h of transfection.
Grow the transfected urinary cells in a hypoxia chamber (5%–6% O2) until human ESC-like colonies appear.
Break hiPSC colonies into a checkerboard-shaped grid using sharp needles under an inverted microscope.
Pick only well-separated and hESC-like colonies to ensure they are clones.
Collect colony pieces using 100-μL pipette tips and transfer them to new Matrigel-coated plates containing fresh TeSR-E8 medium supplemented with 10 μM Y-27632.
Replace the needle and tip each time a colony is picked.
Coat the Matrigel plates freshly before use, preferably 0.5–1 h prior to use.
Reconstitute both oligos to 100 μM using nuclease-free water.
Phosphorylate the two oligos at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Anneal the phosphorylated oligos by heating to 95°C for 5 minutes and then cooling to 25°C at a rate of 5°C per minute.
Digest the pX330 plasmid using BbSI at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Purify the digested pX330 plasmid using a 1% agarose gel and QIAquick Gel Extraction Kit.
Detect the concentration of the digested pX330 plasmid using NanoDrop device.
Set up a ligation reaction with the purified pX330 plasmid and sgRNA.
Incubate the ligation mixture at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 10 minutes.
Transform the product of the ligation into competent cells according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Keep LB agar plate with colonies at 4°C for no more than one month after sealing.
Extract plasmid DNA containing the target sequence using QIAGEN EndoFree Plasmid Maxi Kit as per the manufacturer's instructions.
Store extracted plasmid DNA at −20°C before use.
Analyze the plasmid DNA using Sanger sequencing.
Amplify donor exon 14 from the normal template for homologous recombination.
Insert a 3.4 kbp HDR fragment carrying a selection cassette of neomycin (G418) into pEASY-Blunt simple cloning vector following the pEASY-Blunt cloning protocol.
Pick only well-separated and round colonies after transformation to ensure they are clones.
Extract plasmid DNA by using EndoFree Plasmid Mini Kit as per the manufacturer's instructions.
Store plasmid DNA at −20°C before use.
Dissociate hiPSCs into single cells with accutase when they reach 70%–80% confluence.
Harvest and count the dissociated cells.
Centrifuge the required number of cells, then remove the supernatant completely.
Mix 2 μg of the constructed pX330 plasmid and 2 μg of the targeting vector in nucleofector solution for genome correction knock-in.
Resuspend the required number of hiPSCs (2–3 × 10^5 cells) in nucleofector solution.
Transfer the cell-plasmid mixture to Nucleocuvette vessels carefully, avoiding air bubbles and ensuring sample covers the bottom of cuvette.
Perform transfection using the 4D-nucleofector system with program CA-137.
After electroporation, gently transfer cells to Matrigel-coated plates containing TeSR-E8 medium supplemented with 10 μM Y-27632.
Coat Matrigel plates freshly before use, 0.5–1 h prior to experiment start.
Transfect cells and wait until they reach 70%–80% confluence.
Add G418 to TeSR-E8 medium at a final concentration of 200 μg/mL for cell selection.
Wash the hiPSCs with DPBS and refresh the medium daily during selection period.
Isolate G418-insensitive hiPSC colonies after selection.
Remove TeSR-E8 medium from cells, rinse twice with DPBS.
Dissociate cells using EDTA solution for 5 min.
Resuspend dissociated cells in fresh TeSR-E8 medium and centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min.
Extract genomic DNA using Cultured Cells DNA Kit according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Amplify genomic DNA using Super-Fidelity PCR Kit with denaturation at 98°C for 30 s, annealing at 60°C for 60 s, and extension at 72°C for 30 s for 35 cycles.
Set the thermal cycler’s heated lid to 75°C during PCR.
Perform an extension for 10 min at 72°C.
Hold the PCR product at 4°C.
Verify the PCR product using Sanger Sequencing.
Remove cell lines from liquid nitrogen and thaw them in a 37°C water bath immediately.
Dilute cells with TeSR-E8 medium in a new tube slowly.
Centrifuge the mixture at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend cells in TeSR-E8 medium using gentle pipetting.
Culture cells in Matrigel-coated 6-well plates containing TeSR-E8 medium supplemented with 10 μM Y-27632, and incubate them after shaking.
Aspirate the medium in the 6-well plates and wash the hiPSCs with DPBS once or twice.
Add 2–3 ml of TeSR-E8 medium to the plate and incubate them.
Passage the hiPSCs when cell confluence reaches 70% or more.
Aspirate the medium from the 6-well plates.
Wash the hiPSCs with DPBS once.
Add 1 mL of EDTA to digest the hiPSCs at 37°C for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the EDTA and resuspend hiPSCs in TeSR-E8 Medium containing 10 μM Y-27632.
Break hiPSC clumps into smaller pieces using gentle pipetting.
Add an appropriate volume of cells into a new Matrigel-coated 6-well plate.
Passage the cells every third or fourth day.
For cell freezing, aspirate the EDTA and resuspend hiPSCs with cell cryopreservation solution.
Transfer hiPSCs in a freezing tube and perform gradient cooling.
Store the hiPSCs in liquid nitrogen until use.
Dissociate hiPSC colonies using a cell dissociation solution at 37°C for 3.5 minutes when confluence surpasses 70%.
Resuspend the cells in differentiation medium.
Break hiPSC clumps into single cells by gentle pipetting.
Count and dilute cells in differentiation medium supplemented with 20 μM Y-27632.
Reaggregate cells in 96 V-bottomed conical wells at a density of 12,000 cells per well in 100 μL volume.
Incubate the plates after shaking.
Aspirate 100 μL of medium from each well on Day 6.
Add 100 μL of differentiation medium supplemented with 20 μM Y-27632 and 1.5 nM hBMP4 to each well.
Incubate the plates in a CO2 incubator.
Aspirate 60 μL of medium from each well on Day 9.
Add 60 μL of differentiation medium supplemented with 20 μM Y-27632 to achieve a lower hBMP4 concentration (final: 27.5 ng/mL).
Incubate the plates in a CO2 incubator.
Aspirate 60 μL of medium from each well on Day 12.
Add 60 μL of differentiation medium supplemented with 20 μM Y-27632 to achieve an even lower hBMP4 concentration (final: 13.75 ng/mL).
Incubate the plates in a CO2 incubator.
Transfer aggregates into a Petri dish.
Cut aggregates into 2 to 3 pieces using a V-Lance Knife.
Aspirate all aggregates into 15-mL centrifuge tubes.
Remove supernatant after aggregates settle at the bottom of the tubes.
Resuspend aggregates in neural retina medium.
Transfer resuspended aggregates into 9-cm non-stick Petri dishes.
Refresh the medium every 5 days and protect the culture from light.
